LevelIntro: Use rice to learn grinding force. The goal is a soft rice flavor without a burnt taste.
SuccessFeedback: The rice tastes soft and clean, with no burnt flavor.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Adjust the force or grinding time a little.
WrongFeedback: The rice does not taste right. Check the force and grinding time.

LevelIntro: Use tea leaves to learn grinding speed. The goal is gentle tea bitterness followed by sweetness.
SuccessFeedback: The tea tastes balanced: light bitterness first, then sweetness.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Adjust the speed or grinding time a little.
WrongFeedback: The tea is too bitter. Check the speed and grinding time.

LevelIntro: Tutorial complete. Challenge levels begin now. Red bean, dried tangerine peel, and rock sugar each change the dessert at a different moment.
SuccessFeedback: The dessert has a clear order: red bean first, citrus next, sweetness last.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Check the order or grinding time.
WrongFeedback: The dessert tastes out of order. Check when each ingredient is added.

LevelIntro: Peanut and black sesame are both nutty, but each one should keep its own roasted edge. Use New Batch to grind them separately.
SuccessFeedback: Peanut and black sesame stay clear from separate preparation, then join cleanly in the final batch.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Make sure each ingredient is ground alone first, then put both powders together at the end.
WrongFeedback: The nutty flavors need separate preparation followed by one final combined grind.

LevelIntro: White pepper, dried tangerine peel, and ginger are all sharp. Prepare any two together, prepare the remaining spice alone, then combine the prepared powders.
SuccessFeedback: The spices stay clear: one paired powder, one single powder, then one final blend.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Make sure any two spices become one powder, the remaining spice becomes another powder, then the prepared powders meet at the end.
WrongFeedback: The spice batches need a clearer structure: two together, one alone, then the prepared powders together.

LevelIntro: A small change in amount can shift how the sesame paste feels.
SuccessFeedback: Black sesame is slightly stronger, and glutinous rice keeps the paste smooth.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Adjust the ratio or grinding time a little.
WrongFeedback: The sesame flavor is not clear enough. Check the ratio and grinding time.

LevelIntro: Sand ginger should be the main flavor. Dried tangerine peel and coarse salt should support it.
SuccessFeedback: Sand ginger is clear, with a little citrus and salt behind it.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Check the force, ratio, or grinding time.
WrongFeedback: Salt or citrus is too strong, and sand ginger is not the main flavor.

LevelIntro: White pepper should stay clear without becoming harsh. Peanut and dried tangerine peel should support it. Grind each ingredient in its own batch and adjust the force for each one.
SuccessFeedback: White pepper is clear, peanut adds warmth, and citrus keeps it light.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Check the separate batches, force, speed, or grinding time.
WrongFeedback: White pepper is too harsh, or the support flavors are too weak.

LevelIntro: Make a layered rice dumpling flavor with red bean, glutinous rice, black sesame, and lotus leaf.
SuccessFeedback: The dumpling flavor has clear layers: sticky rice leads, sesame supports it, red bean sits lighter, and lotus leaf finishes at the end.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Check the ratio, grouping, order, or time.
WrongFeedback: The layers are unclear. One flavor may be too strong or added at the wrong time.

TargetTasteName: Force Speed Ratio And Order Challenge
LevelIntro: Yangjiang douchi should be the main savory flavor. Ginger, dried tangerine peel, and salt should support it.
SuccessFeedback: Douchi is the main savory flavor, with ginger, citrus, and light salt behind it.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Check one process or structure setting.
WrongFeedback: Salt, ginger, or citrus is too strong, or the douchi flavor is unclear.

LevelIntro: Make a balanced ginger-scallion sauce. Ginger flavors should lead, with scallion and salt kept light.
SuccessFeedback: The sauce is balanced: light salt, strong ginger, and fresh scallion at the end.
CloseFeedback: Very close. Check the final ratio, grouping, order, force, or speed.
WrongFeedback: The sauce is unbalanced. Ginger may be harsh, scallion may be lost, or salt may be too strong.
